subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type, TPS targets, concurrency, token mix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finedge.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated sizing)

Alex — great to chat this morning. Quick recap of what you shared and a couple of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated appropriately:

Summary of your workload:
- Primary use case: real-time customer support assistant + enterprise analytics queries (hybrid prompts).
- Expected steady-state TPS (text generation requests): ~120 TPS average across business hours, with brief spikes to ~250 TPS for product launches.
- Typical concurrency target: 30 simultaneous long-lived chat sessions; peak concurrent inference requests may reach ~90 for short bursts.
- Token mix: average request length ~350 input tokens, average generated tokens ~160 (so ~510 tokens per call on average). 95th percentile can be ~1,500 tokens for long analysis runs.
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 600ms for interactive flows; background analytics can tolerate higher latency.
- Data constraints: must stay in US region; no on-prem required today but security review ongoing.

Open Qs for us to size:
1) GPU family preference: are you targeting A100-like throughput for cost-efficiency or lower-cost A10G instances? Any existing infra constraints?
2) Do you expect customers to use streaming responses widely (affects memory / KV cache)?
3) Do you have a strict single-tenant requirement (Dedicated reserved capacity) vs a private VPC?

Next steps:
- Alex to confirm preferred GPU family and confirm burst profile (daily/hourly cadence).
- I’ll loop in SE (Soojin) to produce an initial Dedicated sizing recommendation and cost estimate; I aim to send that by EOD PST.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated sizing)

Thanks Marissa — perfect notes and thanks for the template. Quick answers below:

1) GPU family: We'd prefer A100 if it's materially better for latency at our scale; cost is important so if A10G with sharding meets p95 targets we'd consider that.
2) Streaming: yes, ~40% of customer interactions will use streaming (short responses), the rest are full-response generations.
3) Tenant model: Dedicated reserved capacity is preferred (predictable performance + compliance). Private VPC is a potential requirement if the security team flags anything during the SOC review, but not required right now.

Burst profile: daily traffic peaks between 11:30–13:30 PST and 17:00–18:30 PST; plan for 3–4x burst capacity for those windows.

Happy to jump back on a quick call if it helps.

— Alex

- GPU family recommendation (A100 vs A10G vs mix)
- Rough node count for steady-state 120 TPS and burst 250 TPS given their token mix (~510 tokens/call)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + next steps (Dedicated sizing) — recommendation draft attached

Marissa / Aditya — attached is an initial recommendation based on FinEdge's profile. Short summary:

- GPU recommendation: recommend mix with A100s for the core low-latency serving fleet (p95 objective) and a smaller pool of A10G nodes for cost-effective background/analytics workloads. This lets us meet 600ms p95 for interactive flows while keeping costs predictable.

- Steady-state capacity: estimate ~8 A100 GPUs in serving configuration (continuous batching + KV caching) to handle 120 TPS at ~510 tokens/call with p95 < 600ms.

- Burst sizing: autoscale up to ~18 A100 GPUs (or equivalently burst to 36 A10G if using a mixed strategy) to absorb 250 TPS peaks (3–4x). Recommend burst policy with quick scale-up on metrics and a staged scale-down to avoid oscillation.

- Concurrency and KV cache: target 30 long-lived chat sessions per node with per-node KV cache sized for ~100k tokens of active context (depends on chat session history retention). With 40% streaming, ensure memory reservation for streaming buffers; add +15% headroom.

- Cost estimate: rough monthly committed cost ballpark provided in attached PDF (marissa_recommendation_v1.pdf).

Attachments: marissa_recommendation_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Happy to iterate — if FinEdge confirms A100 preference we can tighten the node count and produce a formal quote and SOC notes.

— Soojin

Subject: Dedicated sizing recommendation + next steps

Alex — thanks for the quick answers and for the patience while we pulled this together. Attached is our initial recommendation (summary below).

Summary recommendation:
- Deployment mode: Dedicated reserved capacity in US region (recommended now; Private VPC if security team requires later).
- GPU mix: primary A100 serving pool (8 A100 steady-state), smaller A10G pool for background analytics and cost-effective burst alternatives.
- Burst policy: autoscale to ~18 A100s (or equivalent A10G capacity) for 3–4x peaks; staged scale-down to avoid overshoot.
- Concurrency & cache: per-node concurrency target ~30 long-lived sessions; KV cache sizing ~100k tokens per node with +15% memory headroom for streaming.
- Next steps: confirm GPU preference (A100 vs A10G) and sign commitment to proceed with formal quote. Once confirmed, SE will produce a formal estimate and we can loop in procurement.

Links: HubSpot deal https://app.hubspot.com/deal/87921 | DocuSign starter: https://docusign.com/finish/ABC123def
